written: 2026-11-18, before any sample was drawn and before any consensus result was scored
idea: Corroboration-gated consensus. Answers that an independent source (the rule engine) corroborates on probe inputs are kept; only the rest get extra model samples, and among all candidates the behaviour with the most independent support is chosen (execution-based minimum Bayes risk with a symbolic prior).

targets.fails_example: the pipeline answer fails the visible example
targets.engine_answer: the pipeline answer came from rule-engine back-inference
targets.uncorroborated: the pipeline answer is a model answer and none of the top-10 engine programs agrees with it on probes
targets.no_probes: the visible example cannot be parsed into arguments

probes.grammar: type-preserving mutations of the visible example's arguments (mylittlellm/rulecoder/consensus.py)

agreement: two candidates agree if at least 3 probes give a value for both and no probe gives different values; a probe on which one side raises is ignored
pool: the pipeline answer, if it passes the visible example
the plain-prompt greedy answer, if it passes and differs
every sample that passes the visible example (identical code merged)
the top-10 rule-engine programs for the example
score: s(c) = (model candidates agreeing with c, c included) / (number of model candidates) + lambda * [c is an engine program or some engine program agrees with c]
tie_break: the pipeline answer first, then model candidates in pool order, then engine programs in rank order
fallback: if the pool is empty the pipeline answer is kept
gate: validation split: no fewer tasks solved than the round-3 pipeline (31 of 45)
test: locked split, once, only after the gate passes; counts only
ablation: lambda = 0 (model candidates only, plain MBR-exec) is reported next to the primary rule on every split, including test
not_tuned: k, temperature, lambda, probes and the agreement threshold are fixed here and are not tuned on any split
